hero.subtitle: 12-Week Student Project
hero.tagline: Solo audio designer on a 6-person student team. Made all the sounds—from bouncy disco music to ridiculous item pickups. We even voiced the grandmas ourselves. Fixed the 4-player audio chaos so UI feedback doesn't disappear when everyone crashes at once.

overview.title: Project Overview
overview.desc: Side-scrolling 1-4 player racing game. It's chaotic, loud, and ridiculous.
overview.role_desc: Audio Designer & Technical Implementer. I did everything audio: recording, sound design, music choice, and implementation. 2 programmers, 3 artists, 12 weeks.
overview.tech_desc: MetaSounds for all SFX. The engine pitch, surface changes, and collisions are all driven by real-time gameplay data. No pre-baked loops.
overview.scope_desc: Solo audio designer. Recorded our own voices for the characters. Built the procedural engine audio system.
overview.result_desc: Released on itch.io. We shipped it.

metasounds.title: MetaSounds System
metasounds.story: I didn't want the engines to sound like looped MP3s. I built a graph in MetaSounds where the kart's pitch and rattle intensity change based on speed. You can hear the difference when you drive from carpet to tiles—the sound reacts instantly.

triggering.title: Audio Architecture
triggering.story: When you have 12 weeks to make a game, you need to know where your audio logic lives. Instead of scattering sound files all over the project, I centralized everything. One manager for UI clicks, one system for engine sounds. Debugging took minutes, not hours.

surface.title: Surface Transitions
surface.story: Sudden switching from carpet to tiles sounded fake and glitchy. I added a quick crossfade—when you change surfaces, the old sound fades out smoothly while the new one fades in. It's a matter of milliseconds, but it makes the driving sound professional, not like chopped samples.

mix.title: 4-Player Chaos Control
mix.story: With 4 players crashing and screaming, important sounds got lost in the noise. I set priorities: if you pick up an item, that sound ducks the collisions for a split second. The 'Wall of Death' boxing bell and the woman's '3, 2, 1' countdown cut through everything. Information always wins over noise.

challenges.title: Challenges
challenges.story: The original boost sound caused lag with 4 players. I replaced it with a synth patch in MetaSounds—same impact, near-zero memory.
